title: Three-Year Corporate Strategic Plan: Growth Ambitions, Market Positioning, Capability Investment Priorities, and Business Unit Performance Milestones
subtitle: Three-Year Corporate Strategic Plan — Growth Ambitions, Market Positioning, Capability Investments & Business Unit Milestones

document_brief.narrative_theme: Over the next three years, the company will reposition around a focused set of growth markets while investing in scalable capabilities to deliver measurable, cross-business-unit performance milestones.

sections.heading: Three-Year Growth Ambitions and Market Positioning (FY2026–FY2028)
key_facts: The plan targets $3.2B in revenue by FY2028 (up from $2.4B in FY2025).
International revenue will increase from 18% in FY2025 to 30% by FY2028.
Market positioning will prioritize Healthcare, Financial Services, and Industrial segments starting Q1 FY2026.

sections.heading: Capability Investment Priorities and Business-Unit Performance Milestones
key_facts: Total capability investment will be $180M over FY2026–FY2028, allocated 45% to Data & AI, 35% to Cloud & Platform, and 20% to Go-to-Market Enablement.
Enterprise gross margin will improve from 41% in FY2025 to 46% by FY2028.
By Q4 FY2027, each business unit will launch 2 new packaged offerings and reduce average sales cycle time from 120 days to 90 days.

sections.heading: Strategic Intent and Market Focus
sections.body: Over the next three fiscal years, Horizon Ridge Holdings will reposition its portfolio around four priority growth markets: digital health platforms, renewable infrastructure services, advanced logistics automation, and mid-market cybersecurity solutions. These segments were selected based on projected compound annual growth rates exceeding 11% and alignment with our existing technical competencies. We will streamline exposure to subscale consumer hardware operations by FY2028 to concentrate capital and leadership attention on scalable, margin-accretive businesses. The objective is to increase group revenue from priority markets from 46% to 72% by the close of FY2029.

sections.heading: Portfolio Realignment and Capital Allocation
sections.body: Capital expenditures over the planning horizon will total approximately $640 million, with 58% directed toward capability expansion in digital platforms and automation engineering. We will divest two non-core regional distribution entities by Q3 FY2028, redeploying proceeds into cloud-native product development and strategic acquisitions in cybersecurity analytics. A disciplined hurdle rate of 14% IRR will guide all new investments. Each business unit will submit semiannual capital deployment scorecards to ensure alignment with enterprise return thresholds.

sections.heading: Capability Investments
sections.body: To support scale and cross-business integration, we will implement a unified data architecture anchored by the Orion Enterprise Platform, targeting full deployment by December 2028. Workforce capability upgrades include reskilling 1,200 employees in AI-enabled operations and recruiting 150 specialized engineers in automation and threat intelligence. Shared services will be consolidated into three global centers of excellence to improve process consistency and reduce duplicative overhead. These investments are expected to improve operating margin by 320 basis points across the group.

sections.heading: Performance Milestones and Financial Targets
sections.body: By FY2029, the company aims to achieve consolidated revenue of $3.4 billion, reflecting a blended CAGR of 9.5%, and an EBITDA margin of 18%. Cross-business-unit collaboration targets include generating at least $210 million in annual revenue from integrated solution offerings. Each division will adopt quarterly milestone reviews tied to customer acquisition rates, recurring revenue ratios, and innovation pipeline velocity. Executive incentives will be weighted 40% toward enterprise-wide performance metrics to reinforce shared accountability.

sections.heading: Governance and Risk Oversight
sections.body: A Strategy Execution Committee, chaired by the COO, will convene monthly to monitor progress against transformation benchmarks and risk indicators. Particular oversight will be given to integration timelines, cybersecurity resilience, and regulatory compliance within healthcare and energy markets. Independent audits of program performance will be conducted annually to validate reported gains and cost efficiencies. Transparent reporting to the Board will occur at each scheduled meeting to ensure corrective action where deviations arise.

structure.full_text:
FY2027–FY2029 Corporate Strategic Plan Overview
Ref: CSP-27-29 | Date: 12 February 2027 | From: Office of the Chief Strategy Officer

Section Strategic Intent and Market Focus
Over the next three fiscal years, Horizon Ridge Holdings will reposition its portfolio around four priority growth markets: digital health platforms, renewable infrastructure services, advanced logistics automation, and mid-market cybersecurity solutions. These segments were selected based on projected compound annual growth rates exceeding 11% and alignment with our existing technical competencies. We will streamline exposure to subscale consumer hardware operations by FY2028 to concentrate capital and leadership attention on scalable, margin-accretive businesses. The objective is to increase group revenue from priority markets from 46% to 72% by the close of FY2029.

Section Portfolio Realignment and Capital Allocation
Capital expenditures over the planning horizon will total approximately $640 million, with 58% directed toward capability expansion in digital platforms and automation engineering. We will divest two non-core regional distribution entities by Q3 FY2028, redeploying proceeds into cloud-native product development and strategic acquisitions in cybersecurity analytics. A disciplined hurdle rate of 14% IRR will guide all new investments. Each business unit will submit semiannual capital deployment scorecards to ensure alignment with enterprise return thresholds.

Section Capability Investments
To support scale and cross-business integration, we will implement a unified data architecture anchored by the Orion Enterprise Platform, targeting full deployment by December 2028. Workforce capability upgrades include reskilling 1,200 employees in AI-enabled operations and recruiting 150 specialized engineers in automation and threat intelligence. Shared services will be consolidated into three global centers of excellence to improve process consistency and reduce duplicative overhead. These investments are expected to improve operating margin by 320 basis points across the group.

Section Performance Milestones and Financial Targets
By FY2029, the company aims to achieve consolidated revenue of $3.4 billion, reflecting a blended CAGR of 9.5%, and an EBITDA margin of 18%. Cross-business-unit collaboration targets include generating at least $210 million in annual revenue from integrated solution offerings. Each division will adopt quarterly milestone reviews tied to customer acquisition rates, recurring revenue ratios, and innovation pipeline velocity. Executive incentives will be weighted 40% toward enterprise-wide performance metrics to reinforce shared accountability.

Section Governance and Risk Oversight
A Strategy Execution Committee, chaired by the COO, will convene monthly to monitor progress against transformation benchmarks and risk indicators. Particular oversight will be given to integration timelines, cybersecurity resilience, and regulatory compliance within healthcare and energy markets. Independent audits of program performance will be conducted annually to validate reported gains and cost efficiencies. Transparent reporting to the Board will occur at each scheduled meeting to ensure corrective action where deviations arise.

Confidential — Internal Strategic Planning Document | Page 1 of 1

structure.heading: Capability Investment Priorities and Business-Unit Performance Milestones
text_content: **Capability Investment Priorities and Business-Unit Performance Milestones**

Over FY2026–FY2028 the company will commit a total capability investment of $180M, purposefully allocated to accelerate strategic priorities. Investment breakdown:
- 45% to Data & AI,
- 35% to Cloud & Platform,
- 20% to Go-to-Market Enablement.
This allocation supports cross-enterprise modernization, prioritizing machine learning productization, scalable infrastructure, and sales productivity tools. Funding will be staged annually with front-loaded spend in FY2026 to de-risk platform foundations and steady-state investments in FY2027–FY2028 for productization and commercialization. All committed amounts are monitored under the corporate investment governance framework.

CD, and integrations with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform to meet latency and compliance targets in FY2026–FY2027. Go-to-Market Enablement focuses on sales tooling, pricing engines, and training for Enterprise Sales and Customer Success teams in FY2026–FY2028 to accelerate conversion and retention.

Performance milestones are anchored to measurable financial and go-to-market targets. Enterprise gross margin will improve from 41% in FY2025 to 46% by FY2028 through operational leverage and higher-margin packaged services. By Q4 FY2027 each business unit—Commercial, Enterprise, and Public Sector—will launch two new packaged offerings and reduce average sales cycle time from 120 days to 90 days. Progress will be tracked in quarterly business reviews with the CFO and BU leaders, using KPIs (pipeline velocity, win rate, average deal size); a strict gating model ties tranche releases to milestone attainment.

structure.heading: Three-Year Growth Ambitions and Market Positioning (FY2026–FY2028)
text_content: Our three-year growth ambition is to deliver $3.2B in revenue by FY2028, up from $2.4B in FY2025, representing a compound annual growth rate of approximately 10.1% across FY2026–FY2028. This target reflects targeted expansion in high-margin services, disciplined pricing, and cross-selling across existing accounts. FY2026 will emphasize execution to close a projected $400M incremental revenue gap in year one, with quarterly reviews and strict governance to ensure trajectory toward the FY2028 target.

Geographic diversification is a core enabler: international revenue is planned to rise from 18% in FY2025 to 30% by FY2028. Actions include market entry acceleration in EMEA and APAC, scaling partner ecosystems, and localizing offerings to meet regulatory and go-to-market requirements. Progress metrics will include international bookings, regional NPS, and percentage of total revenue; milestone reviews occur at the end of each fiscal quarter beginning Q2 FY2026.

Market positioning will prioritize Healthcare, Financial Services, and Industrial segments starting Q1 FY2026, with tailored value propositions, dedicated account teams, and regulatory compliance roadmaps. Go-to-market initiatives will include strategic alliances with systems integrators, targeted thought leadership, and segment-specific product roadmaps. Success will be measured by segment revenue growth, win rates against tier-1 competitors, and attainment of defined share objectives by end of FY2028.
